column1: Seldom is the weather more dramatic than when thunderstorms strike.
column2: 很少有哪种天气像雷暴来袭时那样惊心动魄。

column1: Their electrical fury inflicts death or serious injury on around 500 people each year in the United States alone.
column2: 单在美国，雷暴猛烈的放电每年就会造成约500人死亡或重伤。
column3: electrical|adj. 电的；由放电产生的

column1: As the clouds roll in, a leisurely round of golf can become a terrifying dice with death - out in the open, a lone golfer may be a lightning bolt’s most inviting target.
column2: 乌云涌来，原本悠闲的一轮高尔夫球也可能变成一场惊险的生死赌局。在开阔地带，独自打球的人可能最容易成为闪电的目标。
column5: round of golf|一轮高尔夫球
column7: dice with death|冒着生命危险的一搏
column8: out in the open|在开阔地带

column1: And there is damage to property too.
column2: 雷电还会造成财产损失。

column1: Lightning damage costs American power companies more than $100 million a year.
column2: 雷电造成的损害每年给美国电力公司带来超过一亿美元的损失。

column1: But researchers in the United States and Japan are planning to hit back.
column2: 不过，美国和日本的研究人员正计划反击。

column1: Already in laboratory trials they have tested strategies for neutralising the power of thunderstorms, and this winter they will brave real storms, equipped with an armoury of lasers that they will be pointing towards the heavens to discharge thunderclouds before lightning can strike.
column2: 他们已经在实验室里测试过削弱雷暴威力的办法。今年冬天，他们将带着一整套激光设备直面真正的风暴，把激光射向天空，争取在雷击发生前让雷云释放电荷。
column9: an armoury of|一整套可用的装备

column1: The idea of forcing storm clouds to discharge their lightning on command is not new.
column2: 让雷云按人的指令放电，这个想法并不新鲜。

column1: In the early 1960s, researchers tried firing rockets trailing wires into thunderclouds to set up an easy discharge path for the huge electric charges that these clouds generate.
column2: 20世纪60年代初，研究人员试着把拖着导线的火箭射入雷云，想为云中产生的大量电荷提供一条易于放电的通路。

column1: The technique survives to this day at a test site in Florida run by the University of Florida, with support from the Electrical Power Research Institute (EPRI), based in California.
column2: 佛罗里达大学运营的一个试验场至今仍在使用这项技术，位于加利福尼亚州的电力研究所（EPRI）为其提供支持。
column4: survives to this day|一直沿用到今天

column1: EPRI, which is funded by power companies, is looking at ways to protect the United States’ power grid from lightning strikes.
column2: 电力研究所由电力公司资助，正在研究怎样保护美国电网免遭雷击。

column1: ‘We can cause the lightning to strike where we want it to using rockets,’ says Ralph Bernstein, manager of lightning projects at EPRI.
column2: 电力研究所雷电项目负责人拉尔夫·伯恩斯坦说：“利用火箭，我们能让闪电击中指定的地方。”
column7: lightning projects|n. 雷电研究项目

column1: The rocket site is providing precise measurements of lightning voltages and allowing engineers to check how electrical equipment bears up.
column2: 在这个火箭试验场，可以精确测量雷电电压，也能让工程师检验电气设备能否经受住雷击。

column1: Bad behaviour.
column2: 不听使唤的闪电
column3: Bad behaviour|不听使唤的表现（小标题）

column1: But while rockets are fine for research, they cannot provide the protection from lightning strikes that everyone is looking for.
column2: 不过，火箭虽然用于研究很合适，却无法提供人们想要的防雷保护。

column1: The rockets cost around $1,200 each, can only be fired at a limited frequency and their failure rate is about 40 per cent.
column2: 每枚火箭约需1200美元，发射频率有限，而且失败率约为40%。

column1: And even when they do trigger lightning, things still do not always go according to plan.
column2: 即便火箭确实引发了闪电，事情仍未必能按计划发展。

column1: ‘Lightning is not perfectly well behaved,’ says Bernstein.
column2: “闪电并不总是那么听话，”伯恩斯坦说。
column4: well behaved|adj. 听话的（此处形容闪电）

column1: ‘Occasionally, it will take a branch and go someplace it wasn’t supposed to go.’
column2: “偶尔它会分出一支，击中本来不该击中的地方。”

column1: And anyway, who would want to fire streams of rockets in a populated area?
column2: 况且，谁愿意在人口聚居的地方接连发射火箭呢？
column5: streams of|接连不断的；一连串的

column1: ‘What goes up must come down,’ points out Jean-Claude Diels of the University of New Mexico.
column2: “射上去的东西总要掉下来，”新墨西哥大学的让-克洛德·迪尔斯指出。

column1: Diels is leading a project, which is backed by EPRI, to try to use lasers to discharge lightning safely - and safety is a basic requirement since no one wants to put themselves or their expensive equipment at risk.
column2: 迪尔斯正主持电力研究所支持的一个项目，尝试用激光让雷云安全放电。安全是基本要求，因为谁也不想让自己或昂贵的设备面临危险。

column1: With around $500,000 invested so far, a promising system is just emerging from the laboratory.
column2: 到目前为止，已投入约50万美元，一套颇有前景的系统刚刚开始走出实验室。

column1: The idea began some 20 years ago, when high-powered lasers were revealing their ability to extract electrons out of atoms and create ions.
column2: 这个想法始于约20年前，当时高功率激光正显现出从原子中剥离电子、形成离子的能力。

column1: If a laser could generate a line of ionisation in the air all the way up to a storm cloud, this conducting path could be used to guide lightning to Earth, before the electric field becomes strong enough to break down the air in an uncontrollable surge.
column2: 如果激光能在空气中形成一条直达雷云的电离通道，就可以利用这条导电通道把闪电引向地面，赶在电场强到使空气击穿、引发失控的电流冲击之前。
column5: all the way up to|一直向上延伸到

column1: To stop the laser itself being struck, it would not be pointed straight at the clouds.
column2: 为了防止激光器本身遭到雷击，激光不会直接对准云层。

column1: Instead it would be directed at a mirror, and from there into the sky.
column2: 激光会先射向一面镜子，再从那里反射到空中。

column1: The mirror would be protected by placing lightning conductors close by.
column2: 在镜子附近安装避雷装置，就能保护镜子。

column1: Ideally, the cloud-zapper (gun) would be cheap enough to be installed around all key power installations, and portable enough to be taken to international sporting events to beam up at brewing storm clouds.
column2: 理想情况下，这种雷云放电装置的造价会足够低，以便在所有重要电力设施周围安装；同时它也要足够便携，能带到国际体育赛事现场，向正在形成的雷雨云发射激光。
column4: cloud-zapper|n. 使雷云放电的装置

column1: A stumbling block.
column2: 一道难关

column1: However, there is still a big stumbling block.
column2: 不过，目前还有一大障碍。

column1: The laser is no nifty portable: it’s a monster that takes up a whole room.
column2: 这台激光器可不是什么小巧的便携设备。它是个庞然大物，足足占了一整个房间。

column1: Diels is trying to cut down the size and says that a laser around the size of a small table is in the offing.
column2: 迪尔斯正在设法缩小设备的体积。他说，一台只有小桌子那么大的激光器很快就会问世。

column1: He plans to test this more manageable system on live thunderclouds next summer.
column2: 他计划明年夏天用真正带电的雷云测试这套更易操作的系统。

column1: Bernstein says that Diels’s system is attracting lots of interest from the power companies.
column2: 伯恩斯坦说，迪尔斯的系统正引起电力公司的浓厚兴趣。

column1: But they have not yet come up with the $5 million that EPRI says will be needed to develop a commercial system, by making the lasers yet smaller and cheaper.
column2: 但电力公司还没拿出这500万美元。电力研究所说，开发商用系统需要这笔钱，以便把激光器做得更小、更便宜。
column4: come up with|设法拿出（资金）

column1: ‘I cannot say I have money yet, but I’m working on it,’ says Bernstein.
column2: “我目前还不能说钱已经到手，不过我正在想办法筹措，”伯恩斯坦说。
column5: working on it|正在设法解决（筹款问题）

column1: He reckons that the forthcoming field tests will be the turning point - and he’s hoping for good news.
column2: 他认为，即将进行的实地试验将是转折点。他希望得到好消息。

column1: Bernstein predicts ‘an avalanche of interest and support’ if all goes well.
column2: 伯恩斯坦预计，如果一切顺利，“关注与支持将纷至沓来”。
column7: if all goes well|如果一切顺利

column1: He expects to see cloud-zappers eventually costing $50,000 to $100,000 each.
column2: 他预计，这种雷云放电装置最终每台需花费5万至10万美元。
column4: cloud-zappers|n. 使雷云放电的装置

column1: Other scientists could also benefit.
column2: 其他科学家也可能从中受益。

column1: With a lightning ‘switch’ at their fingertips, materials scientists could find out what happens when mighty currents meet matter.
column2: 如果有了随手就能操纵的闪电“开关”，材料科学家就能弄清强电流接触物质时会发生什么。
column3: at their fingertips|可随时取用或操纵

column1: Diels also hopes to see the birth of ‘interactive meteorology’ - not just forecasting the weather but controlling it.
column2: 迪尔斯还希望看到“互动气象学”诞生，不仅能预报天气，还能控制天气。

column1: ‘If we could discharge clouds, we might affect the weather,’ he says.
column2: “如果我们能让云层放电，或许就能影响天气，”他说。

column1: And perhaps, says Diels, we’ll be able to confront some other meteorological menaces.
column2: 迪尔斯说，或许我们还能应对其他一些气象威胁。

column1: ‘We think we could prevent hail by inducing lightning,’ he says.
column2: 他说：“我们认为，通过引发闪电，也许可以防止下冰雹。”

column1: Thunder, the shock wave that comes from a lightning flash, is thought to be the trigger for the torrential rain that is typical of storms.
column2: 雷声是闪电产生的冲击波。人们认为，它会引发暴风雨中常见的倾盆大雨。
column5: is thought to be|被认为是

column1: A laser thunder factory could shake the moisture out of clouds, perhaps preventing the formation of the giant hailstones that threaten crops.
column2: 用激光制造雷电的装置有可能震落云中的水分，或许还能阻止威胁农作物的巨大冰雹形成。

column1: With luck, as the storm clouds gather this winter, laser-toting researchers could, for the first time, strike back.
column2: 如果运气好，今年冬天雷雨云聚集时，携带激光设备的研究人员或许能首次展开反击。
